A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpeakerSleuth, retaining the core 1,818-instance benchmark, four source datasets, and three principal tasks. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine LALMs and six embedding configurations, including detection, localization, discrimination, and reference/context ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds results for twelve LALMs, extended evaluation conditions, and a human-annotated voice-cloning ranking study.

M1.justification: Discrimination gains a complete-ranking output mode, with embedding judges sorting their existing similarity scores rather than only selecting the best candidate. Appendix C also introduces a per-turn LALM reference-comparison procedure. The original benchmark construction and embedding computations are largely retained.

E1.justification: The four original datasets remain, but evaluation expands to complete candidate ranking, longer dialogues containing ten target-speaker turns, and four-candidate voice-cloning quality ranking against human judgments. These add task requirements and input conditions beyond v1's original evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds Gemini-2.5-Pro, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and Audio-Flamingo-3 to the main comparisons and ablations while retaining the nine earlier LALMs and six embedding configurations. The stronger Gemini comparators materially broaden the comparison and lead several evaluations. Table 5 also includes a random baseline for the new voice-cloning task.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Balanced Accuracy and Balanced F1, equally weighting consistent and inconsistent cases, and evaluates ranking using NDCG@1, NDCG@2, and Exact Match. New protocols include per-turn reference comparison, a 759-instance ten-turn benchmark, and a 485-sample human-ranked voice-cloning evaluation. Localization Exact Match reporting is removed. Candidate randomization and the primary five-turn setting were already present in v1.

E4.justification: New analyses test whole-dialogue versus per-turn judging, dependence on FreeVC using CosyVoice3/OpenVoice/YourTTS alternatives, generalization to longer dialogues, and performance by clip-duration quartile. The existing threshold sensitivity and separate context/reference ablations remain. The combined textual-context-without-reference condition reported in v1 is no longer reported.

E5.justification: Section 7.4 newly reports inter-annotator reliability for voice-cloning rankings: three annotators, 50 shared samples, and Kendall's W = 0.860. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or seed-based variability for model performance.

E6.justification: Retained classification results change substantially: GPT-4o-audio's Bazinga accuracy changes from 84.4% to 50.2%, and Reference (ECAPA) on DailyTalk changes from 0.0% to 76.2% in Table 2. Qwen2.5-Omni-3B and Qwen3-Omni S2/S3 localization values are interchanged. v2 adds extensive ranking, robustness, and downstream results while removing earlier detailed breakdowns. Table 1 revises total speakers from 152 to 197 with unchanged per-dataset counts. These are reported revisions, not established performance improvements.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the ranking assumption S1 > S3 > S2, assigns relevance scores 2/1/0, and defines balanced aggregation for detection and localization. Existing embedding and localization mathematics is largely retained or restated. Neither version develops substantive theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central benchmark and modality-imbalance claims remain. The claimed discrimination capability broadens from selecting the best candidate to selection and ranking. The conclusion also replaces the categorical holistic-versus-fine-grained explanation with difficulty in turn-level analysis and explicitly identifies calibration, fine-grained reasoning, and modality integration as challenges.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes indiscriminate localization biases from meaningful acoustic sensitivity in stronger Gemini models, describes embedding detection as comparable under balanced scoring, and identifies complementary strengths in best-candidate selection versus full ranking. New analyses support interpretations about dialogue context, conversion systems, duration, and difficulty matching human voice-cloning judgments. Reference dependence and the attention explanation are qualified, while v1's explicit voice-conversion fidelity limitation is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code/data release promise with an availability statement and repository address, supplies new ranking/per-turn/voice-cloning prompts, and documents the conversion-model mixture. Parameter information is revised. Some dataset-specific segment-sampling rules and annotation-interface documentation disappear. Hardware, temperature, and embedding thresholds were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: References are added for CosyVoice3, OpenVoice, YourTTS, Audio-Flamingo-3, Gemini-2.5-Pro, and Spokenus. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to speaker recognition and existing evaluation approaches remain largely unchanged; bibliographic date updates do not constitute new positioning.

P1.justification: Beyond the title and front-matter edits, v2 extensively condenses existing dataset, verification, embedding-method, and metric descriptions. It reorganizes experimental setup and appendices and substantially rewrites the results narrative and prompt presentation. This is substantial restructuring of retained material as well as expansion.

P2.justification: Table 2 is extensively redesigned with additional metric groups, and the separate context/reference tables are merged. New threshold-bias and duration-analysis plots and several experimental tables appear. The annotation-interface screenshots are removed, detailed appendix tables are replaced by consolidated displays, and prompts change from narrow column boxes to full-width figures.

improvement.justification: Balanced scoring, stronger comparators, and human-ranked voice-cloning evaluation make v2 more informative. However, retained scores change without explanation, granular results and sampling details disappear, and the claimed controlled conversion comparison has an unresolved inconsistency: Appendix D.1 says only inconsistent audio changes, yet Pairwise (ECAPA) S1 accuracy changes from 36.0% in Table 2 to 26.9% in Table 9. These reporting issues limit confidence in the expanded evidence and temper the overall gain.
